title: EDiR Practice Set 5 · musculoskeletal, paediatric and urogenital imaging
subtitle: Radform original · abbreviated EDiR-style practice · English
disclaimer: Simulacro original de Radform basado en la estructura publicada del EDiR. No contiene preguntas oficiales ni bancos de pago.

questions.question: Which MRI findings support vertebral osteomyelitis/discitis? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Infection may involve endplates, disc and paravertebral/epidural soft tissues.

questions.question: Which ultrasound findings may occur in ovarian torsion? Choose all that apply.
options: Reduced or absent flow, although preserved flow does not exclude torsion
questions.explanation: Torsion is diagnosed by integrating ovarian morphology, vascular findings and clinical presentation.

questions.question: Ultrasound is useful in paediatric hydronephrosis primarily to:
options: Assess collecting-system dilatation and renal parenchyma
questions.explanation: Ultrasound provides a radiation-free assessment of the urinary tract.

questions.question: Early stress injury of bone is often most sensitively detected with:
options: Plain radiography within the first few hours in every case
questions.explanation: MRI can detect marrow oedema before a fracture line becomes radiographically visible.

questions.question: Which ultrasound features favour a simple ovarian cyst? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: These are typical benign sonographic features of a simple cyst.

questions.question: PI-RADS assessment of the prostate principally integrates:
options: T2-weighted imaging, diffusion and dynamic contrast according to zone/context
questions.explanation: Multiparametric prostate MRI relies primarily on T2 and DWI, with DCE used in defined circumstances.

questions.question: Whole-body MRI is particularly sensitive for detecting:
options: Bone marrow infiltration by metastatic disease
questions.explanation: MRI is highly sensitive to marrow replacement and can survey the skeleton without ionising radiation.

questions.question: Which ultrasound appearances are typical of intussusception? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: Characteristic concentric and pseudokidney appearances support the diagnosis.

cases.title: Distal ureteric obstruction
cases.stem: Non-contrast CT shows a distal ureteric stone and ipsilateral hydroureteronephrosis.

questions.question: What is the principal diagnosis?
options: Obstructive uropathy due to ureteric calculus
questions.explanation: A ureteric stone with upstream dilatation indicates obstruction.

questions.question: Which CT feature would suggest a complication requiring urgent clinical attention in the appropriate context?
options: Marked perinephric inflammatory change in a febrile septic patient
questions.explanation: Infection combined with obstruction is a urological emergency.

cases.title: Acute paediatric scrotum
cases.stem: A 15-year-old boy presents with sudden severe unilateral testicular pain and nausea. Doppler ultrasound is performed.

questions.question: Which finding most strongly supports testicular torsion?
options: Markedly reduced intratesticular flow compared with the contralateral testis
questions.explanation: Reduced perfusion in the appropriate clinical setting is highly concerning for torsion.

questions.question: Which additional sign may be seen?
questions.explanation: The whirlpool sign of a twisted cord is a direct sign of torsion.

cases.title: Testicular torsion
cases.stem: An adolescent presents with sudden testicular pain. Ultrasound shows an enlarged heterogeneous testis with markedly reduced perfusion.

questions.question: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Acute pain with markedly reduced perfusion is highly suspicious for torsion.

questions.question: What is the appropriate reporting priority?
options: Immediate communication because testicular viability is time-dependent

questions.question: Which response would be potentially unsafe?
options: Reporting the examination as normal despite clear signs of torsion
questions.explanation: A missed torsion can result in irreversible testicular infarction.

cases.title: Spinal epidural abscess
cases.stem: A diabetic patient has fever, severe back pain and progressive leg weakness. MRI shows an enhancing epidural collection.

questions.question: What is the principal diagnosis?
questions.explanation: An epidural collection with infection and neurological deficit is highly concerning for abscess.

questions.question: Which features should be assessed?
options: Neural compression, craniocaudal extent and associated spondylodiscitis
questions.explanation: Extent and neural compromise determine urgency and treatment planning.

questions.question: Which omission would be potentially unsafe?
options: Failing to communicate cord/cauda equina compression from an epidural abscess
questions.explanation: Neurological injury may become irreversible if decompression/treatment is delayed.
